thread:
oncall-bot: PagerDuty alert: P0 - inference-prod: elevated 5xx rate (traffic-split v2 enabled). Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/inference-5xx

maya: Seeing spike ~30% 5xx on /v1/generate since 11:28 UTC. Canary was 10% traffic.

devon: On it. Anyone started the canary rollout today?

sam: I kicked off v2 canary at 11:25 as part of the gated deploy (small config change to sidecar env).

iris: Quick check: kubectl get pods -n inference-prod | grep v2-canary
```
inference-model-v2-canary-5f7d8   1/1     CrashLoopBackOff   5          11m
inference-model-v2-canary-5f7d9   0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   4          10m
inference-model-v2-canary-5f7da   1/1     Running            2          9m
```

sam: Logs from one of the crashloop pods:
```
E0325 11:27:45.123 controller.go:98] failed to attach device: nvidia: no devices available
E0325 11:27:45.124 model-loader.go:201] failed to map model binder config: env MODEL_BINDER_PATH not found
```

devon: Hmm two issues: device plugin errors (maybe node drain moving GPUs?) and env var misconfig in new sidecar (MODEL_BINDER_PATH).

maya: Also seeing kube events: node gke-prod-gpu-23 was drained for maintenance at 11:20 UTC, tainted NoSchedule for 7m. Some pods rescheduled and couldn't find GPUs.

john: Confirming HPA for v2 has minReplicas: 0 in the manifest? That would allow scale-to-zero if metrics hiccup.

sam: `kubectl get hpa inference-model-v2 -n inference-prod -o yaml` shows: minReplicas: 0, maxReplicas: 10, metrics: custom/memory. Looks like autoscaler backoff + traffic spike -> flapping.

iris: Customer impact: traffic-split sends 10% to v2. When pods crash, kube routes back to v1 but for some clients (sticky sessions / dedicated routes) saw 5xx. Estimated 8-12 customers saw intermittent failures.

devon: Immediate mitigation steps proposal: 1) flip feature flag traffic_split_v2 -> 0% (kill-switch) 2) scale v1 up to handle surge 3) cordon & uncordon gke-prod-gpu-23 if needed 4) patch v2 manifest to fix MODEL_BINDER_PATH and set minReplicas:1 before re-rollout.

maya: Agreed. I'll flip the FF and scale v1 now.

maya: (exec) `curl -X POST https://flags.redwood/api/toggle -d '{"flag":"traffic_split_v2","pct":0}'` -> 200 OK :white_check_mark:

sam: Scaling inference-model-v1 to handle extra traffic: `kubectl scale deploy inference-model-v1 --replicas=12 -n inference-prod` -> scaled.

oncall-bot: Traffic rebalanced to v1. Error rate dropping. Monitoring: 5xx falling from 30% -> 1.5% over 3m.

devon: I'm going to cordon gke-prod-gpu-23 and drain any leftover pods, then bring it back.

devon: (exec) `kubectl cordon gke-prod-gpu-23` -> cordoned. `kubectl drain gke-prod-gpu-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` -> completed. Node uncordoned and gpu-plugin restarted.

sam: Patch ready: update sidecar env MODEL_BINDER_PATH and change HPA minReplicas:1. I'll prepare a canary PR but won't flip the flag until we validate.

iris: Customer comms note: notify impacted customers that we mitigated a brief canary rollout issue, they may have seen transient 5xx between 11:25-11:32 UTC. ETA for full postmortem: EOD.

maya: Handoff: I'm going offline in 15m. Leo, can you take on-call for this incident and watch the rollout PR?

leo: Taking it. I'll verify after Sam merges PR and will run a small canary at 1% then 5% if stable.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by leo. Pager duty escalation disabled (on-call transition)

devon: Action items for postmortem: - remove minReplicas:0 pattern from all inference HPAs - add preflight check to avoid canary during node maintenance windows - add FF kill-switch automation to revert traffic immediately on >5% 5xx sustained for 1m - test device plugin resilience during node drain

maya: Thanks team. I'm marking this P0 -> mitigated. Will attach logs and commands to the incident ticket.

oncall-bot: Incident state: mitigated. Opened ticket INC-2025-1123. Estimated customer impact: 12 customers, ~7 minutes peak, no data loss.

leo: I'll keep the ticket and reassign for a full blameless postmortem.

maya: Handing off slack thread to leo for follow-ups. :wave:
